title: CI observability journal record (v1)
description: One line of an append-only JSON Lines journal. Each worker process writes its own journal file, named after its journal_id. Sequence numbers are per journal and contiguous from 1; blank lines are violations, not silently dropped. Starts are recorded immediately, so an interruption leaves a useful partial record: a phase, fixture, or operation with no finish record keeps its last observed state and counts as interrupted or unknown.

journal_id.description: Identity of the journal file this record belongs to. The file is named {journal_id}.jsonl.

invocation_id.description: Identity of the native process invocation this record belongs to, when one job runs several (for example pytest plus Ansible targets, or Go test plus Ginkgo). Must have an invocation_started record in the same bundle.

sequence.description: Per-journal sequence number, starting at 1 and contiguous.

recorded_at.description: UTC wall-clock time at which this record was written.

source_at.description: UTC time of the underlying event according to its source, for records converted from a native report. Absent means the record was observed live.

mono_ns.description: Monotonic clock of the writing process in nanoseconds, or null when unknown. Native reports carry no monotonic clock: converted records use null plus duration_ns on finish records, never a fabricated clock. Clock domains never merge by default: records are only compared within one clock_id, and one journal carries one clock.

clock_id.description: Identity of the monotonic clock domain. Distinguishes which process's clock mono_ns comes from when records from several processes are compared.

clock_uncertainty_ns.description: Bound on the uncertainty of the recorded times, in nanoseconds, for cross-host events.

data.description: Event payload. The event field selects which payload applies.

execution_started_data.description: Job-level opening record. Its job identity and suite must equal the manifest's; the suite is the declared cohort, which may use framework 'mixed' when the job's invocations run several frameworks.

execution_finished_data.description: Terminal record of an execution. outcome is the producer's own observed result, an untrusted claim: GitHub owns the authoritative CI conclusion. inherited is not claimable here; trusted reconciliation assigns it to jobs that were not re-run in a later attempt.

exit_code.description: Process exit code, or null when the process was lost.

failure.description: First observed failure. A cleanup failure never overwrites it.

invocation_started_data.description: Opening record of one native process invocation in the job, with its actual framework context. One job can mix frameworks (for example AAP pytest plus Ansible targets); the job-level suite stays the declared cohort and never claims that every record shares one framework.

dependencies.description: Real dependencies the invocation needs, for example kind, postgres, or envtest. A job named unit may use a real database; its invocation records that.

invocation_finished_data.description: Terminal record of one native invocation, with the child process exit outcome.

exit_code.description: Child process exit code, or null when the child was lost.

collection_finished_data.description: Terminal record of test collection for one invocation. Completed capture is separate from availability of the counts: on a collection error the outcome is 'error' and the counts stay null rather than being guessed. A completed collection with collected_count 0 is a measured empty selection, not a failure. Count and membership checks run only for completed collections; a bundle may be complete with no collection record at all, for example a build failure before any test collection.

collected_count.description: Number of collected tests, selected plus deselected. Required and non-null when the outcome is completed; 0 means measured empty.

deselected_count.description: Number of collected tests the selection deselected.

test_collected_data.description: One test found by collection, before or after deselection. When collection completed, executed tests must be collected and not deselected; selected-but-never-run tests are legitimate (fail-fast, deselection at runtime) and are not evidence loss.

test_id.description: Full safe test identity. Must not contain secrets or raw parameter values.

deselected.description: True when the selection filtered this test out.

test_phase_started_data.description: Start of one phase of one test attempt, recorded live by an instrumented framework. attempt_index counts attempts of the same test_id within this execution: in-job retries and campaign repetitions are new attempts.

test_phase_finished_data.description: Finish of one phase, recorded live. Native framework outcomes are preserved as observed in the phase they occurred in: expected failures and skips can appear in setup or even teardown, and a teardown can time out. The overall attempt outcome is derived from all phases, never stored beside them.

test_result_data.description: Native test result as a report or adapter states it, without fabricating phase boundaries the report does not contain. result_scope distinguishes a per-attempt result from the aggregate final result of a test. Aggregate durations must never be charged to the final retry: an aggregate record carries the total, attempt records carry their own measured spans, and null means unknown, never zero. A test attempt must not be represented both by phase records and by a native attempt result.

attempt_index.description: Attempt this result belongs to. Required for attempt scope, null when unknown.

attempt_count.description: Total attempts the native source reports, for example Ginkgo NumAttempts. Retained without inventing per-retry records; null when unknown.

worker_id.description: Worker that produced the result, or null when the report does not say.

duration_ns.description: Native duration of this result. For an aggregate this is the total across attempts, never the final retry's span.

source_started_at.description: Start time from the native report. Omitted when the source does not provide it.

source_ended_at.description: End time from the native report. Omitted when the source does not provide it.

fixture_started_data.description: Start of one phase of work on one fixture instance. fixture_instance_id groups the setup pair, the use edges, and the teardown pair of the same instance, so two parameterized instances of one fixture stay separate. The setup-to-teardown span is the instance lifetime, including idle time while tests consume it.

fixture_id.description: Dotted fixture identity, for example tests.conftest.default_subnet.

params_fingerprint.description: Safe parameter identity for a parameterized fixture, as a hash. Raw parameter values are never recorded.

fixture_finished_data.description: Finish of one phase of work on one fixture instance. The outcome belongs to that phase only; a finalizer failure never overwrites the setup outcome.

fixture_used_data.description: Edge from a fixture instance to one consuming test attempt. Shared fixture cost is recorded once and linked through these edges, so no giant dependent list is needed at setup time.

operation_started_data.description: Start of a bounded wait or other tracked operation. name is an allowlisted helper name, not a command line. test links the operation to the test attempt that caused it; parent_operation_id is the only dependency link between operations, and it must reference an operation that started in the same invocation without forming a cycle. The journal that carries the record identifies the acting worker.

name.description: Allowlisted operation name, for example wait_for_provision.

expected_condition.description: Safe description of the condition waited for.

parent_operation_id.description: Explicit dependency link to an operation in the same invocation.

operation_progress_data.description: Intermediate progress of a running operation. Only bounded, safe summaries; never arbitrary polled values or command arguments.

observed_state.description: Safe observed state summary, for example a resource phase.

observed_count.description: Safe count of observed items, for example ready pods.

operation_finished_data.description: Terminal record of an operation. When it repeats the resource of its start record, the two must agree.

resource_observed_data.description: One observation of one resource, from a watch or a snapshot. Strictly allowlisted identity, metadata, and status fields: no specs, no labels or annotations, no IP, MAC, or network data, no Secret or ConfigMap bodies, no log payloads. Missing optional fields mean not observed; a deleted observation carries deleted=true rather than disappearing. Details the observer could not read stay absent, never guessed.

deleted.description: True when the observation recorded the resource's deletion.

ready.description: Observed readiness, when the kind has a single readiness notion.

restart_count.description: Observed restart count, when the kind has exactly one.

status.description: Observed status phase or state field.

containers.description: Observed per-container status of a pod, init containers included.

replicas.description: Observed replica status of a controller resource.

warning_events.description: Observed Kubernetes warning events for the resource.

collection_state_data.description: Health of one collection source. Emitted periodically as a heartbeat and once terminally; a complete bundle's every reported source has a terminal record. dropped_records is measured: 0 means nothing was dropped. omitted_fields names contract fields this source could not fill. Not every source is available in every bundle: an absent source is a coverage gap stated by the producer, not a violation.

complete.description: True when the source covered its full interval.
